 Judgment

This appeal is directed against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.54/2017 dated 20.09.2018 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, and MACT-II, Bagalkot by the petitioners claiming enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, we refer the parties as their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It was the case of appellants/petitioners before the Tribunal that petitioner No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the younger brother of the deceased Mounesh Basappa Badiger.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mounseh, on 16.07.2016 was going on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-29/X- 4562 from Shikkeri to Mudhol of Bagalkot district.
He met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA.25/F-2000 by its driver.

As a result of the impact,
Mounesh sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injures.
4. It was further contended by the petitioners that, Mounesh was aged about 20 years.
He was serving as a carpenter in BVV Sangha, Bagalkot and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Petitioners were depending upon him.
With these reasons the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.36,70,000/-.
5. Respondent has denied the case of petitioners.
It had contended that due to negligent riding of the motor cycle by the deceased, accident was taken place and prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. Petitioners have examined PW-1 and got marked Ex.P-1 to P-7 and respondent has examined RW-1.
8. The Tribunal appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record, by the impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.9,92,000/-under the following heads:

Sl.No. Heads Amount  (Rs)
 1 Loss of dependency 9,72,000/-
 2 Towards rituals & funeral expenses 15,000/-
 3 Towards conveyance and 5,000/-
 transportation of dead body
We have heard the arguments of the learned advocate for the appellants as well as the respondents.

10. Following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether appellants/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought?
ii) What order?

11. The learned advocate for the appellants vehemently contends that the Tribunal has not considered Ex.P-7 issued by BVV Sangha, wherein the deceased was serving as a carpenter and ignoring the same, the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at the rate of Rs.9,000/- per month.

The Tribunal has not considered the future prospects of the deceased while awarding the Smt.Drakshayani W/O Basappa Badiger vs The M.D.N.W.K.R.T.C on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27866961/
3 compensation.

entities.text: Smt.Drakshayani W/O Basappa Badiger vs The M.D.N.W.K.R.T.C on
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has also awarded a meager sum towards loss of consortium and not at all awarded compensation under the head loss of estate.
Therefore, prayed to award just and reasonable amount of compensation.
12. The learned advocate for the respondents supported the impugned judgment and prayed to modify the rate of interest @ 6% per annum.
13. The Tribunal on the basis of the available evidence has held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.
The said finding is not challenged by the respondents.
Therefore, there is no need of reconsidering the same.
14. It is not in dispute that deceased was aged about 20 years at the time of the accident.
The appellants have not proved salary certificate-Ex.P-7 in accordance with law.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly rejected the contention of the appellant that the deceased was drawing salary of Rs.15,000/- per month as per Ex.P-7.
The Tribunal, has held that deceased might be earning Rs.300/- per day as wages by carpentry work.
It does not for call for any interference.
The Tribunal failed to consider the future prospects of the deceased.
The deceased died at the age of 20 years.
As held in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40% of his income has to be considered towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly deceased was unmarried.

Therefore, 50% of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The net income on which the appellants might be depending upon is, Rs.6,300/- per month.
Undisputedly, the multiplier applicable in the present case is 18.

Considering the same, the amount of compensation for which the petitioners are entitled under the head loss of dependency is Rs.6300x 12x 18=Rs.13,60,800/-.
16.
The petitioners are also entitled for compensation under the conventional heads.
Petitioner No.1 being the mother of the deceased lost her young son, aged about 20 years and petitioner No.2 is minor and younger brother has lost the love and affection of the deceased.

As held in the case of Pranay Seti (supra), and Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 Supreme Court Cases 130 and so also in the case of N.
Jayashree and others v. Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance Company Ltd., reported in AIR 2021 Supreme Court 5218, Rs.44,000/- each is to be awarded towards loss of consortium to the petitioners.

17. Rs.16,500/- each is awarded to the petitioners towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

18.
The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum.
The same is on the higher side.
Even the banks do not grant interest at the rate of 9% on fixed deposit kept for a period of one year.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount of compensation.
19. For the aforesaid discussion, we pass the following ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.
Both parties shall bear their own costs.
Impugned judgment passed in MVC No.54/2017 dated 20.09.2018 is modified.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,81,800/- as against Rs.9,92,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

The petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,89,800/- with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum on the said amount from the date of petition till payment of the said amount.
Respondents are directed to pay the said amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.
Remaining part of the impugned judgment is kept intact.
